You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Step-by-step diagnosis:

1. The failing test calls RandomStringUtils.random(3, 0, 0, false, false, new char[]{'a'}, new Random(seed)) and expects the result "aaa".
2. In the method, lines 231-238 check if start == 0 and end == 0, and then set end based on if letters and numbers are false or true.
3. Since letters and numbers are false, end is set to Integer.MAX_VALUE.
4. On line 241, gap = end - start is calculated, which in this test will be Integer.MAX_VALUE - 0 = Integer.MAX_VALUE.
5. On line 248, when chars != null, it tries to select a character as chars[random.nextInt(gap) + start].
6. The problem is that gap is very large (Integer.MAX_VALUE), but chars array length is only 1 (contains only 'a').
7. Thus random.nextInt(gap) can produce a random number much larger than chars.length, causing ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
8. The code incorrectly uses gap for the random index into chars on line 248, instead of using chars.length as the bound.
9. The current bug report comment shows the problem line ch = chars[random.nextInt(gap) + start]; and suspects this results in exception when end or chars array is invalidly passed.
10. The test fails because the method logic calculating the range for random index into chars is incorrect if chars is supplied but start==0 and end==0 parameters are given.

Summary: The root cause is that when the user passes start=0 and end=0 and a chars array, line 248 computes random.nextInt(gap)+start where gap = end - start (Integer.MAX_VALUE) instead of using chars.length as the bound. This results in an attempt to index chars out of bounds and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The test expects the output "aaa" because chars is {'a'} and the random selection should only pick from chars array indexes, but because of the incorrect calculation using gap instead of chars.length, an exception occurs.

The fix should ensure that when chars array is supplied (not null), the random index for accessing chars is generated based on chars.length only, ignoring gap/end/start parameters that are meant for generating characters from a range. This prevents out-of-bound indexing.

Recent bug reports do not mention this issue, so they are not relevant here. The current report correctly identifies the problematic code line and symptom. The failing test specifically triggers this with start=0, end=0, chars={'a'} parameters.

Therefore, the bug is caused by misuse of the random index bound in the method when chars array is supplied with start and end set to 0, leading to an incorrect very large gap used as the bound and subsequent out-of-bounds array access.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test fails because RandomStringUtils.random is called with parameters (3, 0, 0, false, false, {'a'}, random). In the method, when start and end are both zero and letters and numbers are false, end is reset to Integer.MAX_VALUE. The variable gap is calculated as end - start, which becomes Integer.MAX_VALUE. Later, when chars array is non-null, the code attempts to select a character by indexing chars[random.nextInt(gap) + start]. Since gap is enormous (Integer.MAX_VALUE) and chars length is only 1, this indexing always goes out of bounds, causing ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The root cause is misuse of gap as the index bound instead of chars.length when chars array is supplied. The fix should be to generate random indices within the bounds of chars.length when chars != null, ignoring gap/end/start values in this case. This explains the failure in the test case, matching the current bug report's description pointing to this exact line and condition.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.lang3.RandomStringUtils.random(int,int,int,boolean,boolean,char[],java.util.Random)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
